title: A repaired threshold
bodyMd:
A fictional museum replaced a worn entrance threshold with a new stone slab. The old slab was uneven, and staff had recorded several near-falls. Some visitors objected that the new surface erased a visible trace of generations entering the building. The museum retained the removed slab in its collection and installed a small display explaining the replacement.

The curator described this as a compromise, not a perfect preservation of the original experience. A stone in a case no longer performs its former role under visitors’ feet. Nevertheless, leaving it in place would have continued an avoidable access problem. The museum’s response distinguished preserving material from preserving use: the former could be partly achieved through collection and documentation, while the latter had to change. The display invited visitors to consider that distinction rather than pretending that every aspect of the past had survived intact.
